messages:
jess: Ran across-region sweep comparing SSE (server-sent events) vs WS (websocket) vs unary (non-streaming) for streaming vs non-stream endpoints. Put slope-of-throughput-vs-p50 plots in the sheet. TL;DR: SSE gives lower p50 for interactive (<200 tokens) but unary/non-streaming gives much higher token throughput when batching >=8.

omar: Nice. which GPUs/regions did you run? batch sizes? seq len?

jess: GPUs: A10G (us-west1), A100 (eu-west1), H100 (ap-southeast1). seq lens: 64 / 256 / 1024. batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16. latency measured client->reply completion (stream end) and we collected p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s.

mira: What about quantized variants (int8/q8_0/q4_0) and kernel choices? any quality regressions?

jess: Ran q8_0 and q4_0. Quality diffs minimal at seq 64/256, slight regressions at 1024 for q4_0 on dialog evals (~1.8% rouge drop on our holdout). Kernel notes: tested Triton fused-attn vs cuBLAS fallback. Fused-attn gives better streaming p50 for seq <= 256 but on H100 long seqs fall back to cuBLAS/fallback kernels -> throughput drop and worse p95.

alyssa: Ops Q: any difference for autoscaling? SSE/WS keep sockets open so capacity pressure is connection-limited vs unary which is throughput-limited?

jess: Exactly. Observed SSE/WS per-connection memory & CPU overhead. On H100 we hit connection limits around ~6k SSE conns per GPU before p99 climbs; unary saturates token throughput earlier when batch tuned (batch=16 gave highest tokens/s). This implies different scaling targets: concurrent_connections vs tokens/s.

omar: Can you paste the slope chart numbers or a tiny table excerpt?

jess: Sure — excerpt from the CSV: 
```
gpu,region,endpoint,seq,batch,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_s
A10G,us-west1,SSE,64,1,85,230,1400
A10G,us-west1,WS,64,1,95,260,1600
A10G,us-west1,UNARY,64,16,210,520,5000
A100,eu-west1,SSE,256,1,150,420,900
A100,eu-west1,UNARY,256,8,540,1200,3600
H100,ap-southeast1,SSE,1024,1,420,980,300
H100,ap-southeast1,UNARY,1024,16,1250,3000,1800
```

mira: So SSE p50 << unary for short seq, but unary tokens/s much higher with batching as expected. Any observed network/regional variance?

jess: Yes. Latency variance larger across regions for streaming endpoints (RTT sensitivity). APAC shows ~1.2-1.5x worse p50 on streaming vs EU/NA due to additional network hops, which pushes some interactive workloads over SLOs. GPU-level: H100 has higher single-request latency for very long seq when kernel fallback happens.

alyssa: Ops implication: should we route interactive features to SSE by default? What about connection-pooling and keepalive tweaks?

jess: Recommendation: interactive -> prefer SSE if target p50 SLO < 250ms and typical seq <= 256. Use WS if you need bidirectional messages or many small incremental edits. For high-throughput background/async generation route to unary with batch tuning + optional q8_0 quantization. Also: increase connection pool limits for A10G clusters and add circuit-breaker on connection growth; autoscaler should track concurrent_connections metric for streaming tiers and tokens/s for unary tiers.

ci-bot: perf-sweep finished: 34 runs failed (mostly socket exhaustion during peak concurrent open/close), infra ticket #5423 opened.

alyssa: Filed autoscale/pcap tweaks and a follow-up to increase per-GPU fd limits. Thanks for the extract, jess! :thumbsup:

omar: Can you upload the raw CSV and chart link?

jess: uploaded -> https://drive.redwood.ai/sheets/benchmark_slope_apr2026 (sheet contains raw traces, charts, and per-run metadata).
